canonical_question: What are the reported microstructural parameters (specifically interparticle spacing of oxide particles and initial powder dimensions) for the CoCrFeMnNi HEA, and does the provided literature establish a quantitative relationship between these parameters, their thermal stability at elevated temperatures, or the volume fraction required to prevent softening?

evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

evidence_spans: Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.

The average diameter of the initial powders was measured as 27.2 um ( d 10 = 17.9 µm, d 50 = 26.1 µm, d 90 = 38.2 µm).

However, there is a consensus on the absence of data regarding the thermal evolution of these features or the critical volume fractions required to alter mechanical behavior.
